transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can I start by asking your name, and what brings you in today?

My name is… well, you can call me Lisa. I guess what brings me in is my eating’s been kind of inconsistent lately. Not terrible, I don’t think, but enough that I noticed it.

Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’ll end up in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed, eating crackers or sweets. It feels a little embarrassing to say, but that’s what finally made me think maybe I should talk to someone.

When you find yourself eating in the middle of the night, does it feel like you're eating a large amount in a short period, and do you ever try to compensate for it by fasting, exercising, or making yourself vomit?

I don’t think it’s, um, a huge amount exactly… at least I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It’s more like I’ll be standing in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep, picking at crackers or sweets, and then I realize I’ve eaten more than I meant to.

I don’t make myself throw up or anything like that. And I’m not really exercising to “make up” for it. Some weeks I just barely eat dinner, though… not always on purpose, my appetite is just kind of all over the place. Does that make sense?
Do you ever feel like you’re not in control while you’re eating these snacks late at night — like you can’t stop or you feel compelled to keep eating even if you don’t want to?

I mean… maybe a little, yeah. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, like I’m completely out of control, but some nights I’ll go in for just a few crackers or something sweet, and then I’m still standing there after everyone’s gone to bed eating more than I meant to.

It’s just been kind of all over the place — some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights it’s like I keep picking at things. That’s really what made me think I should come in.
When you find yourself eating late at night, does this usually happen after you’ve already gone to bed and woke up, or are you still up and about when it happens?

I’m usually still up, I think. Not like I’ve gone to bed and then wake up specifically to eat.

It’s more after everyone else has gone to bed, and I’m still kind of wandering around or standing in the kitchen, and I’ll end up eating crackers or sweets. It’s not every night, but that’s been part of what made me feel like my eating’s been all over the place.
Do you usually have much of an appetite in the morning, or do you find yourself not really wanting to eat until later in the day?

In the mornings… I don’t always have much appetite, no. It kind of varies, but I’ve noticed my eating is just really uneven lately.

Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed, eating crackers or sweets. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult about it or anything… it just feels all over the place, and that’s part of why I thought I should come in.
Do you usually have much of an appetite in the morning, or do you find yourself not really wanting to eat until later in the day?

Yeah… I guess I don’t always want much in the morning. It’s not that I’m trying not to eat or anything, it’s just kind of uneven.

Honestly, what made me think I should come in is that my eating’s been all over the place — some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets. It feels a little embarrassing saying it, but… that’s been happening.

Has this pattern of eating been causing you a lot of distress, or has it affected your daily life in any way, like making it hard to focus, affecting your relationships, or changing how you feel about yourself?

I wouldn’t say it’s ruining everything or anything like that… but it has been bothering me, yeah.

I think what finally pushed me to come in is just that my eating has been so all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers and sweets. It makes me feel kind of embarrassed and not really like myself, if that makes sense.
How often would you say you end up eating more than you meant to — like when you go into the kitchen intending to have just a few crackers but end up eating a lot more?

Um… not every night or anything. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But it does happen sometimes, mostly at night. I’ll think I’m just going to have a few crackers or maybe something sweet, and then I realize I’ve eaten more than I meant to. It’s been part of that whole pattern I mentioned — some weeks I barely want dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating more than I planned. It’s embarrassing, but… yeah, that’s been happening.
When you find yourself eating more than you meant to, do you tend to eat very quickly or until you feel uncomfortably full?

I don’t think it’s usually to the point where I’m painfully full or anything… at least, I try not to let it get like that.

It’s more that my eating feels kind of out of rhythm. Some weeks I barely want dinner, and then other nights, after everyone’s in bed, I’ll be in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets and I realize I’ve had more than I meant to. I don’t know if that counts as “very quickly,” but it does feel a little out of control in the moment, and then I feel embarrassed afterward.
When you end up eating more than you meant to, would you say you’re eating a definitely larger amount than most people would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances?

I’m not totally sure how to judge that, honestly. I don’t think it’s some huge amount every time… I don’t want to exaggerate it.

It’s more like my eating is just really inconsistent. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights, after everyone’s gone to bed, I’ll be standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets and realize I’ve had more than I meant to. Maybe that’s more than someone else would have in that moment, I’m not sure… it just feels embarrassing because it doesn’t feel like me.
Do you find yourself eating these late-night snacks in secrecy because you feel embarrassed about how much or how often you're eating?

Yeah… I guess I do, a little. I don’t really think of it as “sneaking,” exactly, but it’s usually after everyone’s gone to bed, and I’m standing in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets. I think part of it is because I feel embarrassed that my eating has been so all over the place — like some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m doing that.

I know it probably sounds silly, but that’s honestly part of what finally made me feel like I should come in.

Has this pattern of eating at night or after everyone else has gone to bed caused you significant distress or affected your ability to function in your daily life, such as at work, school, or with family and friends?

It’s caused me some distress, yes… I don’t know if I’d say it’s completely ruined my day-to-day functioning or anything like that. I can still get through things.

But it’s been bothering me enough that it’s part of what finally pushed me to come in. My eating just feels all over the place — some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets. And afterward I feel embarrassed, like, “Why am I doing this?” So… yes, it does upset me, even if I try to tell myself it’s not that big of a deal.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially around the time these eating patterns started or got worse?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because it’s not like something awful happens every day. But I do have these stretches where everything in the house just feels kind of gray and heavy.

I’ll be sitting at the kitchen table feeling empty, and I can’t even point to anything terrible that happened that day. It just feels like that. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… yes, I think that’s been around when the eating gets worse.
Would you say that feeling down or hopeless happens most days and lasts most of the day, even when nothing particularly bad has happened?

I think… yes, during those stretches it does feel like it’s most of the day. I don’t want to overstate it, because I can still do little things and act normal enough, but the house just feels gray and heavy, and I’ll sit at the kitchen table feeling empty even when nothing bad really happened.

Is that what you mean by down? Because it’s not always dramatic, it’s more like this heaviness that just stays there.
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with family, or other things that used to make you feel good?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I still try to keep up with things, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve stopped everything, but things I used to look forward to can feel more like chores now.

Like book club, cooking, going to galleries… even tending the rose beds. Those used to feel good, or at least calming, and lately I’ll just keep putting them off. I tell myself I’m just tired or busy, but it’s more like I don’t get the same feeling from them. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you been feeling a lack of energy or fatigue most days, even when you haven’t done anything particularly tiring?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I get tired, but I haven’t really noticed it as a clear “most days” kind of thing, if that makes sense.

Sometimes I’ll say I’m tired when I don’t want to do something, but I don’t know if that’s real fatigue or just… not feeling very motivated. I don’t want to say yes if that’s not quite right.
Do you find yourself feeling badly about your body shape or weight, especially in relation to these eating habits you’ve been describing?

A little, yes… I don’t want to make it sound like I’m obsessed with my weight or anything. It’s more that I feel embarrassed about how inconsistent it’s been.

Honestly, that’s part of what finally made me come in. My eating has been all over the place—some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’ll be in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed, eating crackers or sweets. And afterward I feel kind of ashamed, like, “Why did I do that?” 

I don’t know if that answers what you’re asking.
Would you say that your low mood or lack of interest in things has been present nearly every day for most of the day, even when your eating patterns are more stable?

I think… yes, at least in stretches. I don’t know if it’s literally all day every day, so I don’t want to overstate it, but there are days where the whole house just feels gray and heavy.

I’ll sit at the kitchen table feeling kind of empty, even when nothing bad has happened that day. And that can be true even if I’ve eaten normally, so I don’t think it’s only about the eating. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been having trouble sleeping — either not being able to fall or stay asleep, or sleeping too much — most days?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really been tracking. I mean, I have the occasional bad night like anyone, where I’m up thinking or I wake up and can’t get comfortable, but I wouldn’t want to say it’s most days if I’m not sure.

I guess my sleep is not perfect, but I haven’t noticed a clear pattern of either barely sleeping or sleeping too much. Is that okay to say?
